source: Cambodia Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), "ប្រព័ន្ធវប្បកម្មដំណាំស្រូវ តាមគោលការណ៍ធម្មជាតិ (ប.វ.ស)" [System of Rice Intensification Following Natural Principles / SRI], 14-page Khmer-language handout/booklet, undated, no author or elibrary URL visible on any page (footer reads "កំរណ៉ការអភិវ័ទ្ធន៍វិស្ស័យកសិកម្ម ខែត្តកំពងចាម" = "Agricultural Extension/Skills Development Office, Kampong Cham province")
text:
The source document lists 12 key techniques of the System of Rice Intensification (SRI) said to be needed for rice to give a good result:

1. Use natural/organic fertilizer, especially compost, to keep the soil fertile.
2. Use pure seed and select only full, well-filled grains for sowing.
3. Build a raised, well-drained nursery bed and sow seed evenly so seedlings emerge uniformly.
4. Pull seedlings carefully, taking them out with care, and transplant each one immediately rather than letting pulled seedlings sit.
5. Transplant seedlings while still young -- less than 15 days old.
6. Transplant carefully with only about 1 seedling per hill.
7. Transplant shallowly and gently; do not push/press the seedling deep into the mud.
8. Transplant in straight rows with equal hill-to-hill spacing.
9. Leave adequate spacing between rows (the source gives a spacing figure in the range of roughly 2.5-4 [unit not fully legible in the source -- likely a hand-span or foot-based traditional unit rather than a metric one; recorded as given without converting, since the exact unit could not be confirmed]).
10. Avoid keeping deep standing water in the field while the rice is actively growing.
11. Remove weeds and aerate/loosen the soil 2-4 times during the growing season to keep air circulating well in the root zone.
12. Keep the soil well-drained, with a system in place for draining excess water out of the field.

Note: technique 9's exact spacing unit was not confidently legible from the source page and is flagged here as uncertain rather than guessed; the 25-40 cm hill spacing given elsewhere in the same document's traditional-vs-SRI comparison table may be the intended figure, but this file records the two separately since they appear as distinct numbers on different pages of the source.
